solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Review various reports etc (10)

annotation.surface: An editor asks for a review of assorted reports and so on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Etc' looks like lazy padding but supplies the letters E, T and C the anagram needs.
annotation.definitionFit: A retrospective look back is a review of what has gone before.

entries.clue: See report of journey here and there (4)

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we want a word that sounds like it

blocks.note: to roam is to journey here and there

annotation.surface: A traveller's account of wandering from place to place.
annotation.walkthrough: The Holy See is the Pope's jurisdiction, based in Rome, so 'See' stands for the city.
annotation.definitionFit: The Holy See, the papal authority, sits in Rome, so a See can stand for it.

entries.clue: ‘Bitter zone’ — name of hellish region (9)

annotation.surface: A grim place-name, 'Bitter Zone', fit for somewhere hellish.
annotation.walkthrough: Tartarus is the pit of the underworld in Greek myth; TARTAREAN is its adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Tartarean means belonging to Tartarus, the hellish region of Greek myth.

entries.clue: A lot become less severe when leader’s gone (5)

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader, is removed

blocks.note: SOFTEN minus its first letter S

annotation.surface: A strict regime that relaxes once its boss departs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A lot' reads as a noun, a large amount, but here it is the adverb: 'I go there a lot'.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something a lot means doing it often.

entries.clue: Dog may show the way ahead (7)

blocks.note: a gun dog breed that aims its nose at game
anything, like an arrow or signpost, that indicates direction

annotation.surface: A dog trotting in front and leading its owner along.
annotation.walkthrough: The pointer breed gets its name from standing still and aiming its nose at game.
annotation.definitionFit: A pointer is both a gun dog and anything that indicates direction.

entries.clue: Part of church taking risk with Latin (7)

blocks.note: to take a chance is to take a risk

annotation.surface: A congregation gambling on keeping the Latin mass.
annotation.walkthrough: The chancel is the east end of a church around the altar, where the choir and clergy sit.
annotation.definitionFit: The chancel is the section of a church around the altar.

entries.clue: Block within this laboratory (4)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words

annotation.surface: A block found inside a laboratory.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters span the join between 'this' and 'laboratory'.
annotation.definitionFit: A slab is a flat, thick block of stone or wood.

entries.clue: Nearly all botanical things go (5)

indicators.note: take all but the last letter

blocks.note: the green parts of a plant, with the final S dropped

annotation.surface: Most of a garden's plants dying off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Botanical things' is a vague stand-in for LEAVES, the parts of a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to leave a room and to go from it are the same act of departing.

entries.clue: Stigma I cast off and flourished (10)

blocks.note: a brand is a mark of disgrace, a stigma
to shed is to cast off

annotation.surface: Someone throws off a stigma and goes on to thrive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flourished' means thrived in the surface but waved about, as with a sword, in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: To flourish a sword is to brandish it, waving it about showily.

entries.clue: Join in tricks and puzzles (8)

indicators.note: the first piece goes in the second

annotation.surface: Taking part in games of tricks and puzzles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Puzzles' looks like a noun beside 'tricks'; it is the verb, as in 'it puzzles me'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to bewilder or leave someone unsure.

entries.clue: Weary male falling over in desert (5)

indicators.note: something that falls over ends up upside down, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: An exhausted man collapsing in the desert sand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desert' is not sand here but what you deserve, as in 'getting your just deserts'.
annotation.definitionFit: Desert, in the sense of deserts, is what one merits or is due.

entries.clue: Before long baddie will acquire a lover (9)

blocks.note: 'in a mo', informal for in a moment
a rat is a nasty person

annotation.surface: A villain who will soon find himself a girlfriend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a mo' is British slang for 'in a moment'. An inamorata is a female lover.
annotation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman someone is in love with, a lover.

entries.clue: Attractive space that’s possessed by our planet? (8,5)

definitions.note: the definition is a description by example: something the Earth has

blocks.note: a field is an open space

annotation.surface: An appealing stretch of open land owned by the Earth.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the Earth has a magnetic field, but so do other bodies.
annotation.definitionFit: The Earth possesses a magnetic field, which is what makes a compass work.

entries.clue: See 12
Man’s crisis could come from such self-interest (10)

indicators.note: one set of letters can be rearranged to come from the other

annotation.surface: A man's troubles blamed on his own selfishness.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a moral: a man's crisis really could come from narcissism.
annotation.definitionFit: Named for Narcissus, who fell in love with his own reflection; self-interest here is a loose gloss on self-love.

entries.clue: Editor has the last word, having got article from Berlin (7)

blocks.note: amen is the last word of a prayer

annotation.surface: An editor overruling everyone after acquiring a piece from Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has the last word' reads as winning the argument, but it means AMEN, the word ending a prayer.
annotation.definitionFit: An editor is one who amends text, an amender.

entries.clue: Clamour before good fellow has good fight (4-4)

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the next

blocks.note: a don is a university fellow

annotation.surface: A noisy good chap winning a fair fight.
annotation.walkthrough: A don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college. A ding-dong is a British informal word for a heated fight.
annotation.definitionFit: British informal: the clanging of bells lends its name to a noisy, evenly matched scrap.

entries.clue: The Parisian boys? You may get them in class (7)

definitions.text: You may get them in class

annotation.surface: French schoolboys, with a hint that you meet such boys at school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You may get them in class' looks like it refers to the boys, but it defines the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Lessons are what pupils are given in class.

entries.clue: Adjust attire, one being sloppy (9)

annotation.surface: Straightening clothes on someone who dresses untidily.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Adjust' suggests tidying the attire, but it means to orientate, to align yourself.
annotation.definitionFit: To orientate is to adjust or align to one's surroundings.

entries.clue: Orthodox minister in charge (7)

annotation.surface: A traditional clergyman running his church.
annotation.walkthrough: IC is short for 'in charge', a common crossword abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Canonic means conforming to accepted rules, orthodox.

entries.clue: Holiday accommodation, home containing old plant (7)

indicators.note: the home word holds the old letter inside it

annotation.surface: A holiday cottage with an old plant pot on the sill.
annotation.walkthrough: A holiday camp is a British seaside resort of chalets; IN takes O to give ION.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the red and white campions are common wild flowers of European hedgerows.

entries.clue: Number going round estate briefly offering fun and gaiety (7)

indicators.note: the number wraps around the next piece
said briefly, estate shrinks to its standard short form, as on a map or address

blocks.note: EST, the short form of estate

annotation.surface: A figure going round an estate, bringing cheer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' in a clue usually means one particular number to be guessed, here a small one.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective for adjective: a party that offers fun and gaiety has the air of a feast day.

entries.clue: Never stopping, king is attacker (7)

annotation.surface: A king who keeps attacking without rest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aye' is an old word for 'always', so 'for aye' means for ever.
annotation.definitionFit: A forayer is one who makes a sudden raid, an attacker.

entries.clue: Fast bowler who is a drug pusher? (5,8)

blocks.note: cricket slang for a very fast bowler
a dealer in speed, the amphetamine

annotation.surface: A cricket fast bowler suspected of dealing drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket, the bowler delivers the ball; a speed merchant is one who bowls very fast. The question mark flags the drugs reading as whimsical.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: cricket slang for a genuinely quick bowler, and, read literally, a trader in the drug speed.

entries.clue: We agreed to shut up this bore (5)

annotation.surface: People agreeing to silence a tedious person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is not a tedious person but a tidal wave running up a river; eagre is another name for it.
annotation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up an estuary.

entries.clue: See 22
After spring, paper’s boss was optimistic (5)

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first

annotation.surface: A newspaper editor feeling hopeful once spring arrives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season; it is a jump.
annotation.definitionFit: Past tense for past tense: expecting a good outcome is being optimistic.

entries.clue: Quiet group in conspiracy (4)

annotation.surface: A silent group involved in a conspiracy.
annotation.walkthrough: P for quiet comes from the musical direction piano.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a secret plan by several people, like the Gunpowder Plot.

entries.clue: Cleverness of northern native enemy ultimately concealing information (9)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of enemy is used
the first piece hides the second inside it

blocks.note: the Inuit are native peoples of the Arctic north
gen is British slang for information

annotation.surface: An Arctic native cleverly hiding intelligence from the enemy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Northern native' is a description, not a place: the indigenous people of Arctic Canada and Greenland.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name the quick, inventive kind of intelligence.

entries.clue: Fruit left for girl (5)

annotation.surface: Some fruit left out for a girl.
annotation.walkthrough: Pearl is a girl's name; crosswords often define names this loosely.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'girl' stands for any girl's name, and Pearl is one taken from the gem.

entries.clue: Suitable get-together (4)

blocks.note: an archaic adjective for fitting or proper
a gathering, as of a hunt or an athletics event

annotation.walkthrough: The adjective 'meet' is old-fashioned, surviving in the prayer book's 'meet and right'.
annotation.definitionFit: Meet is an old word for fitting, and a meet is also a gathering.

entries.clue: Contents of green tin I’d poured out as part of recipe (10)

indicators.note: we use the letters the words contain
the letters tip out in a new order

annotation.surface: Emptying a can of something green into a dish while cooking.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a kitchen scene, so the tin's contents seem to be the ingredient; really the letters are.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: each item on a recipe's list is one of these components.
